LESSON: VOLUME AND CAPACITY

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.3 Area (8 lessons) • square metre (m2 ), acres, and hectares as u
Topic 3.4: Volume and Capacity

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Volume and Capacity. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify metre cube (m3 ) as a unit of volume in measurements
2. identify the relationship between cm3 , m3 and litres in real-life situations

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: VOLUME AND CAPACITY
Volume and Capacity is a Grade mathematics skill used at school, at the market, and at home.

HOW TO STUDY THIS TOPIC
1. Read each idea slowly.
2. Copy every worked example into your book and recalculate it yourself.
3. Then try the practice questions without looking at the answers.

WORKED EXAMPLE STYLE
Write the question clearly. Show each step. Box the final answer.
Example framework:
  Question: (write a Volume and Capacity problem)
  Step 1: …
  Step 2: …
  Answer: …

KENYAN CONTEXT
Use shillings, market goods, school desks, or garden plots as story numbers so the maths feels real.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Solve one simple Volume and Capacity question using objects or a drawing.

Example 2: Solve a harder Volume and Capacity question showing every step.

Example 3: Make a word problem about Volume and Capacity set at a Kenyan market.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write and solve five questions on Volume and Capacity.
2. Explain one solution aloud to a parent or friend.
3. Invent one new word problem and solve it.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Complete 10 practice questions on Volume and Capacity in your exercise book.
2. Mark your work. Redo any question you missed.
3. Teach a younger learner one method from this lesson.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify metre cube (m3 ) as a unit of volume in measurements
2. identify the relationship between cm3 , m3 and litres in real-life situations

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
